Mindgut · reach569 exchanges · 29 aug – 23 oct 2026 · one record

What the record already holds.

Mindgut keeps every exchange between Julia and Mir. These six plates are printed from that record: each shows one measured thing a context window cannot know. Scroll.

↓ six plates · printed by the T-04 effect set

Plate 01 · the ink runs out

The longer they talk, the less is new.

One roller, inked once at the top, never re-inked. Each line is one exchange; the ink's pressure is the share of its words the record had never seen before. First fifty exchanges: 33% new. Last fifty: 1.6%. The record has learned its own vocabulary.

printing
Reading it. Solid at §1 because everything was new. By §500 the roller is dry: 97 words in 100 have been said before. The pale bars are attachments and errors (nothing said).
roller · FX-02 · pressure = novelty
run-out along record order
after U-07 all-day poster
Plate 02 · the window

Seven exchanges hold half. The record holds nearly all.

Of the words in your next exchange, how many are already in what the model can see? A model sees the last seven: 53%. The whole record: 89%. The gap is the product, as one number. Each bin is a count of dots; the ember bin is the window.

printing
Reading it. Still climbing at 100, nearly flat at 569. That shape is the signature of a thing with a finite, learnable structure. The record is not noise and not infinite. It is a person.
stipple · FX-01 · 1 dot = 1 word in 1 000
six bins · ember = the 7-window
after U-24 instrument dial
Plate 03 · the long returns

Some words come back after five hundred exchanges.

Every time a word is reused, it is usually within the week. But 1 in 8 returns come after a silence of more than fifty exchanges. premises was said at §4 and not again until §968. A window cannot make that recall. These are the ones only the record can make.

printing
Reading it. Each thread is one word; it leaves at the exchange where it was last said and lands where it returns. The longest are labelled. Hover a thread.
thread · one direction out, one back
length = the silence
after U-04 embroidery standard
Plate 04 · who is driving

The conversation runs on her words.

In an exchange, Mir uses 27% of Julia's words. Julia had already said 10% of Mir's. Each disc is one exchange, stitched in two directions: the upper half is Julia's share, the lower Mir's. Where the halves run the same way the mark disappears.

printing
Reading it. The eight empty discs at the start are API timeouts: Mir said nothing in Julia's words because Mir said nothing. The record carries its own outages. Hover a disc.
satin · two directions, one thread
angle between halves = clash
after U-04 · U-21
Plate 05 · the seeds

The roots are all at the start.

An exchange that introduced words the rest of the record went on to use is a seed. §2 introduced words that 514 later exchanges reused; §4, §14, §55 and §34 follow. Almost every root is in the first sixty exchanges. Tone is forward reach: the darker the site, the more of the record grew from it.

printing
Reading it. Tone is a head count: 1 dot = 4 later exchanges that reused this one's words. Everything of substance said before §950 has been returned to at least once. No old orphans.
stipple · FX-01 · 1 dot = 4 exchanges
key: the same pen at five values

Plate 06 · a thought

Type something. See where it already lives.

Every exchange is a dot, placed by record order and what it shares with the others. A thought is a fix: the exchanges that answer it rise as bins that run out at the tip. The box is the seven a model sees.

thought
printing
Reading it. Usually none of what rises is in the box. That is the whole point: the model would have answered without it.
stipple at rest · pen dots when risen
ember = answers · dotted = their order
after U-24 · U-32
How to read these. Every mark is a count: one dot is one exchange, one word, one return. Ink is laid by the T-04 effect set's roller and stipple ramp on a fine paper tooth, lit by one sheet light; no gradient stands in for a material. Words are stemmed (stippled → stipple) and stop-words removed. The clash angle is Fisher–Rao on the phase simplex. Matching on plate six is keyword, not the engine's reach.
Rooted in U-07 all-day poster, U-06 atlas plate, U-24 instrument dial, U-04 embroidery standard, U-23 title slide.
